analysis:
Examined the MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift units: the base excerpt (1018-1606) and the head excerpt (1-528). The visible head excerpt stops before most of the changed ranges: lines 743, 865 and 1208 onward are not in the head text, and the only patch hunks shown are partial. Per the patch excerpt, the changes are: (1) passing `modelType` into the reasoning-prefix/content-seed probe at the two call sites (~743, ~865); (2) a new `streamedCalls: prepared` argument to `NativeToolStreamRouter`; (3) a new `router.streamsToolCalls` terminal branch (~1399-1431) that settles tool calls already streamed as deltas and re-checks the set; (4) edits near 1479-1483 and 1517-1548. The patch excerpt for (3) is truncated, and the new router code lives elsewhere.

Security-relevant observations from visible context: the existing release and cancel paths (OneShotRelease fire, cancelUpstream, native lease handoff, first-content deadline checks) are unchanged in the visible lines. Tool-call streaming as deltas means calls are exposed before final validation. The patch comment says each call is validated when its frame closes and the whole set is re-checked at the end, so `ToolConstraintValidation.validate` and `formatOutput?.validate` must still run in the streaming path. The visible base code gates this on the final `toolCalls` array. If the new branch skips `toolHandler?.finish()` / `ToolConstraintValidation.validate` for streamed calls, required or named tool-choice enforcement and response_format validation could weaken. That cannot be confirmed from the supplied lines. Because the model output handled here is adversarial-provider-side, this is an output-integrity matter (T-007) rather than a confidentiality one. The change does not touch the encryption, attestation, cache-scope or lease boundaries (T-008, T-041, TB-011).

No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence. The next pass should read the head text for lines 1208-1548 and the NativeToolStreamRouter streamedCalls implementation. It should confirm that streamed-call paths still apply tool-choice validation and response-format checks, still release via releaseBox on every exit, and keep the native media terminal-drain semantics (nativeMediaTerminalDrain) intact.
